title: दार्चुलेली भाषामा ऊर्जावत् पदसङ्गति (Conjugation in Darchuleli Language)
nepali: दार्चुलेली मातृभाषा नेपालको सुदूरपश्चिम प्रदेशको नेपाली मातृभाषा हो । गढवाली, कुमाउनी, दार्चुलेली मातृभाषा पहाडी भाषा हुन् । नेपाली मातृभाषालाई परम्परागत रूपमा पूर्वी पहाडी भाषा भन्न सकिन्छ तर कुमाउनी र दार्चुलेली, बैतडेली, डडेल्धुरेली महाकाली वारिपारि बोलिने भाषा हुन् । ‘भाषा र भाषिका’ भन्ने शब्द समाज भाषा विज्ञानका पारिभाषिक शब्द हुन् । राजनीतिलाई अघि नसारी कुनै पनि मातृभाषालाई ‘भाषा’ हो कि ‘भाषिका’ भनेर छुट्ट्याउन सकिदैन । डेभिड क्रिस्टल (सन् २००३) ले के भनेका छन् भने जुन भाषालाई राष्ट्रिय झण्डा र सेनाले परिभाषित गर्छ, त्यो चाहिँ भाषा हो भने, जुन भाषा राष्ट्रिय झन्डा र सेनाले सुसज्जित हुँदैन, त्यो ‘भाषिका’ हो । यसरी हेर्दा महाकाली नदी वारिको दार्चुलेली र महाकाली पारिको कुमाउनी एउटै भाषा हो तर नेपालको सिमानाभित्र पर्ने हुनाले दार्चुलेली चाहिँ पछिल्लो राजनीतिक परिवर्तनभन्दा अगाडिसम्म नेपालीको भाषिका मानिन्थ्यो भने कुमाउनी अहिले पनि हिन्दीको भाषिका मानिन्छ । ग्रिर्यसनकै दृष्टिमा नेपालीभन्दा बढी पश्चिम पहाडी, केन्द्रीय पहाडी अरू सबै पहाडी भाषा जस्तै दार्चुलेली भाषा भारोपेली आर्य भाषा हो । प्रस्तुत लेखको उद्देश्य दार्चुलेली भाषाको भूत र अभूत कालमा रहेको ऊर्जावत्वको पदसङ्गतिगत अध्ययन गर्नु रहेको छ । उल्लिखित उद्देश्य पूर्तिका लागि गुणात्मक अनुसन्धान विधिको प्रयोग गरिएको छ । यस लेखका लागि दार्चुलेली मातृभाषाका वक्ताहरूबाट प्राथमिक सामग्री सङ्कलनका साथै भाषा र व्याकरणका सैद्दान्तिक पुस्तकहरूलाई प्रयोग गरी द्वितीयक तथ्याङ्क सङ्कलन गरिएको छ । उल्लिखित अध्ययनमा दार्चुलेली भाषामा क्रियाको पदसङ्गति र नामको पदसङ्गति ऊर्जावत् छ । अकर्मक क्रिया चाहिँ कर्तासँग हुन्छ भने सकर्मक क्रिया कर्मसँग हुन्छ । कर्मको पछाडि विभक्ति आयो भने चाहिँ र कर्मसँग पनि नभई क्रियाको अन्य पुरुष एकवचन हुन्छ, मानवेतर जन्तुसँग पनि त्यस्तै पसदङ्गति हुन्छ । यसमा कोटिकार र लिङ्गको पनि प्रयोग हुन्छ । दार्चुलेली भाषा भूत र अभूतमा ऊर्जावत् रहेको छ । यस लेखबाट भाषा व्याकरणका क्षेत्रमा काम गर्ने विधार्थी, शिक्षक, अनुसन्धाताले लाभ लिन सक्ने अपेक्षा गरिेएको छ ।
american_english: The Darchuleli mother tongue is a Nepali mother tongue of the Sudurpaschim Province of Nepal. Garhwali, Kumauni and Darchuleli mother tongues are hill languages. The Nepali mother tongue can traditionally be called an eastern hill language, but Kumauni and Darchuleli, Baitadeli and Dadeldhureli are languages spoken on both sides of the Mahakali. The words 'language' and 'dialect' are technical terms of sociolinguistics. Without pushing politics to the front, no mother tongue can be sorted out as a 'language' or a 'dialect'. David Crystal (2003) has said that the language which a national flag and an army define is a language, whereas the language that is not outfitted with a national flag and an army is a 'dialect'. Looked at this way, Darchuleli on this side of the Mahakali River and Kumauni on the other side of the Mahakali are one and the same language, but because it falls inside Nepal's border, Darchuleli was considered a dialect of Nepali right up until the latest political change, while Kumauni is still considered a dialect of Hindi. In Grierson's view as well, the Darchuleli language, like the western hill languages beyond Nepali, the central hill languages and all the other hill languages, is an Indo-European Aryan language. The aim of the present article is to study the energic agreement found in the past and non-past tenses of the Darchuleli language. A qualitative research method has been used in order to fulfill the objective stated above. For this article, along with the collection of primary material from speakers of the Darchuleli mother tongue, secondary data has been collected by using theoretical books on language and grammar. In the study noted above, verb agreement and noun agreement in the Darchuleli language are energic. An intransitive verb goes with the subject, while a transitive verb goes with the object. If a case marker comes after the object, then, and even when it is not with the object, the verb is in the third person singular; with non-human animals the same agreement occurs. Number and gender are also used in this. The Darchuleli language remains energic in the past and the non-past. It is expected that students, teachers and researchers working in the field of language and grammar can take benefit from this article.
british_english: Darchuleli is a Nepali mother tongue belonging to the Sudurpaschim Province of Nepal. The Garhwali, Kumauni and Darchuleli mother tongues are hill languages. By tradition the Nepali mother tongue may be termed an eastern hill language, but Kumauni, together with Darchuleli, Baitadeli and Dadeldhureli, are languages spoken on either bank of the Mahakali. 'Language' and 'dialect' are technical terms of sociolinguistics. Unless politics is brought into the foreground, no mother tongue can be distinguished as being a 'language' or a 'dialect'. David Crystal (2003) observes that the speech which a national flag and an army define is a language, whereas the speech that is not furnished with a national flag and an army is a 'dialect'. Viewed in this way, Darchuleli on this bank of the Mahakali River and Kumauni on the far bank of the Mahakali are one and the same language, yet because it lies within Nepal's frontier, Darchuleli was reckoned a dialect of Nepali until the most recent political change, while Kumauni is reckoned a dialect of Hindi even now. In Grierson's eyes too, the Darchuleli language is an Indo-European Aryan language, like the western hill languages beyond Nepali, the central hill languages and every other hill language. The purpose of this article is to carry out a study of the energic agreement found in the past and non-past tenses of the Darchuleli language. A qualitative research method has been employed for the fulfilment of the objective set out above. For this article, primary material has been collected from speakers of the Darchuleli mother tongue, and secondary data has been gathered by using theoretical books on language and grammar. In the study set out above, verb agreement and noun agreement in the Darchuleli language are energic. An intransitive verb agrees with the subject, whereas a transitive verb agrees with the object. Where a case ending follows the object, then — and not agreeing with the object either — the verb takes the third person singular; with non-human creatures the agreement is of the same kind. Number and gender, too, are employed here. The Darchuleli language is energic in the past and the non-past. It is to be hoped that students, teachers and researchers engaged in the field of language and grammar may derive benefit from this article.

'Language' and 'dialect' are technical terms in sociolinguistics. You can't sort any mother tongue into 'language' or 'dialect' without dragging politics into it first. David Crystal (2003) reckons that the speech a national flag and an army define is a language, while the speech that doesn't come with a national flag and an army is a 'dialect'. Going by that, Darchuleli on this side of the Mahakali River and Kumauni on the other side are the same language, but since it sits inside Nepal's border, Darchuleli got treated as a dialect of Nepali right up until the last political shake-up, while Kumauni still gets treated as a dialect of Hindi. By Grierson's reckoning too, Darchuleli is an Indo-European Aryan language, same as the western hill languages past Nepali, the central hill languages and every other hill language. This article sets out to look at the energic agreement in the past and non-past tenses of the Darchuleli language. A qualitative research approach has been used to meet that objective. For this article, primary material was collected from Darchuleli mother-tongue speakers, and secondary data was put together using theory books on language and grammar. In the study above, verb agreement and noun agreement in Darchuleli are energic. An intransitive verb hooks onto the subject, while a transitive verb hooks onto the object. If a case marker turns up after the object, then — and not stuck to the object either — the verb goes third person singular; non-human animals take the same agreement. Number and gender get used here as well. Darchuleli comes out energic in both the past and the non-past. The hope is that students, teachers and researchers working in language and grammar get something out of this article.

translator_notes: ऊर्जावत् is a grammatical term for the energic mood and is kept as 'energic' throughout. अन्य पुरुष एकवचन rendered 'third person singular'. Source typos (पसदङ्गति, गरिेएको, विधार्थी) left uncorrected, as the abstract is not reproduced here.
